item.description: The NFL's back in London, innit?
item.content:encoded:
The NFL heads back to London in Week 4 to play the third international game of the season, featuring the Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to serve up fans a healthy dose of the NFL along with their morning coffee.

Both the Colts and Commanders enter the week with a 1-2 record, putting an air of importance on this game despite being so early in the season, as each team looks to avoid falling to 1-3, where playoff chances grow increasingly slim.

The Commanders will notably be without starting quarterback Jayden Daniels for the second consecutive week as he makes his return from a dislocated elbow suffered in Week 2. He traveled with the team and returned to practice in a limited fashion before head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Friday that backup Marcus Mariota would start in his place. Mariota will also be down his top wide receiver, as Terry McLaurin was ruled out with a hamstring injury.

How to watch Colts-Commanders in London Week 4

Colts-Commanders start time: 9:30 a.m. ET
Location: Tottenham Hotspur Stadium | London
TV channel/live stream: NFL Network, NFL+

item.title: Keys before kickoff: Cowboys at Texans Week 4
item.description: Today is very important.
item.content:encoded:
The 1-2 Dallas Cowboys travel to the 0-3 Houston Texans this week. Here are the keys to the game.

Keep Dak Prescott clean

The Houston Texans pass rush is brutal for opposing quarterbacks. They’re currently ranked fourth in the NFL in sacks and eighth in pressure rate while blitzing at just the 25th highest percentage across the league. Their front four are getting home to take down quarterbacks without much help from blitzing linebackers or defensive backs.

Leading the charge for the Texans front is Will Anderson Jr. The fourth-year player is currently Pro Football Focus’ second-highest rated edge, posting a grade of 93.0. His pass rush win rate through three weeks sits at 22 percent even though he’s facing double teams 41.5 percent of the time. And to top it all off, he also has a 91.1 run-defense grade that ranks him amongst the best edges in the NFL versus the run. Anderson Jr. is a complete player who can wreck games on multiple fronts.

Terence Steele will have his hands full this week since Anderson Jr. lines up on the offense’s right side a majority of the time. The right tackle has had his share of struggles this season, and the Cowboys are well aware. Steele has been left on an island at a lower rate than any other offensive tackle this season. Expect Dallas to continue to provide help to their struggling tackle.

On the other side, Tyler Guyton has been a pleasant development for the Cowboys. He’ll be tasked with predominantly blocking the other edge, Danielle Hunter. While he’s no slouch, Hunter is not the same caliber player as his teammate on the other side of the line. With the Texans’ linebacker depth stretched to a breaking point, expect Dallas to test the offensive left when running the ball early on. If successful, this could be a game where they neutralize Will Anderson Jr. by playing keep away all day.

Surviving Nico Collins

Another week, another dominant NFL player coming off injury to torture the Cowboys. Or at least that’s the plan for Nico Collins and the Texans.

Collins injured his hamstring in practice on September 16th and has been out for the last two weeks. He was a full participant on Friday and now has no injury designation heading into the matchup. And boy did this team need their star wide receiver.

In week one, with Collins in the lineup, the Texans put up 31 points on the Buffalo Bills. In the two weeks without him, they scored six against Cincinnati and 17 against Indianapolis. He’s a key cog in the wheel for the Houston offense and they’ll be getting him back just in time to face a beat up Dallas secondary.

One player to keep an eye on in this matchup is the newly acquired Joey Porter Jr. The new star cornerback in Dallas is set to make his debut in a Cowboys uniform after miraculously recovering from a back injury that plagued him all off season and through the first three weeks of the NFL season.

While he will surely be on a pitch count this week, the last time Porter Jr. and Collins faced one another, the defensive back won the day allowing just two catches for 17 yards on five targets. Four of those were considered tight window throws.

With as challenging as this system can be from a communicative perspective, the plan should not be to utilize the new corner in much zone this week. While the zone-match concept works well for what he brings to the table, he’ll need a few weeks to ramp up. This week, look for Porter Jr. to be locked up on Collins on money downs. He’s best used as a physical, man corner – so put him in and let him do what he does best.

Finish the game

Last week in Rio, the offense and defense both played well enough to win the game. But in the last 28 seconds, with victory just a fingertip away, the head coach didn’t seem to understand if he was playing to win, to go into overtime, or to lose. That cannot happen again.

This winless Texans team is rabid. They are foaming at the mouth for a win. And the last thing you want to do is approach a cornered animal while unprepared.

Even though they are without a win, Houston has a ton of things to like about this matchup. Will Anderson Jr. versus Terence Steele could be a disaster for Dallas. Nico Collins comes back this week to play against an extremely banged up secondary. The Texans struggling offensive line has a chance to get right versus a Dallas pass rush that’s been worse than lackluster this season.

If the Cowboys can find the answers to these problems, they should be the team that walks out of Reliant stadium with the win. If not, it’ll be another long (yet short) week in Dallas.

item.title: Marcus Mariota leaves Week 4 with right knee injury with Commanders already without Jayden Daniels
item.description: The Commanders are already without starting quarterback Jayden Daniels in Week 4.
item.content:encoded:
The Washington Commanders came into Week 4 dealing with multiple significant injuries on offense. Early in the contest, they were dealt another one, as quarterback Marcus Mariota was forced to leave the game after a first-quarter sack.

The play occurred on Washington's second drive of the game. With the team deep in Indianapolis Colts' territory, Mariota was sacked on a third-and-goal. The Commanders were forced to kick a field goal at the end of the drive, taking a 6-0 lead.

Mariota headed to the blue tent on the sideline before being taken back to the locker room. The Commanders eventually announced a right knee injury for Mariota. He was deemed questionable to return.

The @Colts get a huge sack on 3rd and goal@INDvsWAS on NFL Network
Stream on @NFLPluspic.twitter.com/orNGwpNKtU

— NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026

On the team's next drive, Athan Kaliakmanis entered the game as the team's starting quarterback. The drive marked Kaliakmanis' NFL debut. The team selected him out of Rutgers in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft.

Mariota's injury comes at an awful time for the Commanders. The team came into Sunday's contest without starting quarterback Jayden Daniels, backup running back Rashaad White and No. 1 receiver Terry McLaurin.

While the Commanders' offense stalled twice with Mariota under center — settling for field goals — the veteran had shown some big-play potential before going down. Prior to leaving the game, Mariota had a 35-yard rush and found running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on a short gain that wound up going for 35 yards.

This story will be updated.

item.description: Detroit Lions vs. Carolina Panthers Week 4 best player prop bets and parlays
item.content:encoded:
After another wild Week 3 victory, the Detroit Lions go back under the lights on the road. They take on the defending NFC South champion, the Carolina Panthers. Carolina is entering the game banged up all over, and with the weather looking like it will have some rain involved, that affects what I am looking at this week. The forecast calls for some rain early in the morning, with thunderstorms on and off from noon until 6 p.m and during the game it’s a decent shot at some more precipitation.

Last week was a great week for my bets, going 3-0 on the straight bets and hitting a parlay if you combined them all into one. The bold bets were hit-or-miss: quarterback Jared Goff did his part, while the other two didn’t.

Let’s keep the hot streak going, as I have three wagers to watch on Sunday evening. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook.

1. Sione Vaki 15+ rushing yards (+120)

Last week against a stout New York Jets defense, backup Lions running back Sione Vaki had a career game, getting six carries for 26 yards. Those stats aren’t impressive, but with this game likely relying on the ground game, I think Vaki will get similar chances as last week. What also helps is facing this poor Panthers run defense.

Carolina has allowed the most rushing yards in the NFL (580), the most yards per carry (5.7), and is tied with the Green Bay Packers for most rushing touchdowns with six. This Panthers defense is struggling to stop the run, so pair that with a rain game where both teams will lean on the run, and chances are the Panthers defense won’t stop Detroit. I think Vaki can hit this because if Detroit runs the ball heavily, Gibbs will need a breather, and Vaki can take those reps.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $22

2. Jahmyr Gibbs over 134.5 rushing/receiving yards(-114)

Similar concept for this pick here as the one above. Detroit will lean on the running game, and Gibbs will get most of the workload against this Panthers defense. The Panthers are struggling to stop the run, and the whole team is dealing with injuries. While Panthers safety Nick Scott and linebacker Devin Lloyd are back after missing last week, Gibbs will test how healthy they really are and will be a mismatch for both through the air.

Just because there will be rain doesn’t mean the Lions will abandon the passing game either. The explosive deep shot throws might not be there, but the short throws and screens will shine. Gibbs will put the Panthers’ defense on their heels with his quickness after the catch to move the ball downfield.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.77

3. Over 50.5 points (-118)

Before knowing the weather, I was easily hammering the over as both offenses are high-scoring units. I was shocked to see that the line is at 51 points, and I still think this is doable. The Lions have averaged 31 points a game this season; I could easily see that number go higher against this Panthers defense.

Carolina’s offense has been impressive too, averaging 29.7 points per game. The Lions’ secondary has struggled this season, so the rain might give them a little bit of ease if it holds up. I think Carolina will still find some success against Detroit, so if the Lions put up 31 points, I can see Carolina scoring 20. Both defenses have struggled this season, and the rain could change up both offenses, but I think Detroit scores enough to do the heavy lifting here.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.47

If you want to turn these three single bets into a same-game parlay, the odds are +511 and $10 -> $51.15

Record: 5-4

Brandon’s Bold Bet

If you want to go bold and build a big parlay that could pay well, put these three bets together in a parlay:

  1. Isaac TeSlaa 20+ receiving yards (+102)
  2. Sione Vaki anytime touchdown (+750)
  3. Most rushing yards Jahmyr Gibbs (-240)

Since being held without a catch in Week 1, Lions wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa has been more involved in the passing game. He tallied 26 receiving yards in Week 2 and 66 in Week 3, so 20 should be doable, even with the rain. With my belief that Vaki will get more carries this week, I see him getting a goal-line carry and finding the end zone for the first time in his career. Finally, I see Gibbs finish the game with the most rushing yards of any player; he’s the best running back on the field on Sunday and is bound to break out some big runs.

I hit one of three of these last week, and this week I leaned into the boldness this week with the Vaki touchdown to amplify the payout. While this seems bold overall, I think this has a chance of hitting, especially if Detroit can have a big lead late in the game.

Odds +2049 and bet $10 -> $214.96

Record: 0-3

Do-it-all parlay

If you want to combine all six plays into a parlay and go big or go home, here are the odds:

  1. Sione Vaki 15+ rushing yards
  2. Jahmyr Gibbs over 134.5 rushing and receiving yards
  3. Over 50.5 points
  4. Isaac TeSlaa 20+ receiving yards
  5. Sione Vaki anytime touchdown
  6. Most rushing yards Jahmyr Gibbs

Odds +6229 and bet $10 -> $632.95

Record: 0-3

Use this information however you like. You can ignore it and watch the game, or, if you want to risk some money, follow these recommendations or test your own luck. Whatever you decide, please gamble responsibly and bet only money you can afford to lose.

The fourth weekend of the 2026 NFL season is here!

Let’s run through a Philadelphia Eagles-focused rooting guide for all of the Week 4 games.

EAGLES GAME

LOS ANGELES RAMS at PHILADELPHIA EAGLES: Beating the Rams would be a big deal. Not only because it prevents the Eagles from dropping to 2-2 … but also because it gives Philly a value head-to-head tiebreaker over LA. Putting the Rams in a 1-3 hole also sounds nice. The Eagles will have to pull off an upset to make it happen. Go Birds.

NFC EAST

INDIANAPOLIS COLTS at WASHINGTON COMMANDERS: The Commanders are 1-2 after Marcus Mariota guided them to an upset win over the other Washington football team last week. Don’t want to see this team build any momentum before Jayden Daniels returns from injury. Root for the Colts.

ARIZONA CARDINALS at NEW YORK GIANTS: The Giants are 2-1. If they win this game, they’ll be 3-1 with some more winnable games coming up. Better to see them not building belief in thesmselves that they can win games without Jaxson Dart. Root for the Cardinals.

DALLAS COWBOYS at HOUSTON TEXANS: The Cowboys are the biggest threat to the Eagles threepeating as division champs. Root for the Texans.

If the Eagles win and all of their division rivals lose, the NFC East standings will look like this:

1) Eagles: 3-1
2) Giants: 2-2
3) Cowboys: 1-3
4) Commanders: 1-3

NFC PLAYOFF PICTURE

NEW YORK JETS at CHICAGO BEARS: Ben Johnson seems to be Vic Fangio’s kryptonite. The Eagles don’t want to see the Bears in the playoffs. Root for the Jets.

GREEN BAY PACKERS at TAMPA BAY BUCCANEERS: Neither team is very imposing but the Packers have the better record (1-2 vs. 0-3). Might as well root for the Packers to lose so that they don’t catch up to the Eagles. Root for the Buccaneers.

MIAMI DOLPHINS at MINNESOTA VIKINGS: AFC team over NFC team, especially with the NFC team being undefeated and ahead of the Eagles in the NFC playoff picture. Root for the Dolphins.

DENVER BRONCOS at SAN FRANCISCO 49ERS: The Niners are looking like a problem. Root for the Broncos.

LOS ANGELES CHARGERS at SEATTLE SEAHAWKS: AFC team over NFC team. Root for the Chargers.

DETROIT LIONS at CAROLINA PANTHERS: The Lions are the bigger threat in the NFC. Root for the Panthers.

ATLANTA FALCONS at NEW ORLEANS SAINTS: The Saints have shown the higher ceiling thus far. They might be the bigger threat. Root for the Falcons.

WHAT’S LEFT

NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS at BUFFALO BILLS: The Eagles own the more favorable of two 2027 fifth-round picks either from the Pats or Bears. Might as well root against New England. Root for the Bills.

item.title: NFL odds, betting, storylines: 3 underdogs to back in Week 4
item.description: Let's look at three spots where some 'dogs are in position to bark.
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes in life, you've got to go against the grain. And in this case, the "grain" is the vast majority of the NFL betting public with my Week 4 NFL underdog recommendations.

Not only am I backing one team that has yet to win a game or cover a point spread, and another team whose quarterback has six more turnovers than touchdown passes, but in both instances I'm fading two squads that are 3-0 SU and ATS.

My third NFL underdog recommendation? Let's ride the only other franchise that — to the shock of most everyone — is off to a 3-0 start on the field and in the wagering department.

Patriots at Bills (-6.5)

The Bills are one of those 3-0 SU and ATS squads. The Patriots, meanwhile, have dropped two of their first three (both on the road), with the latest being an atrocious performance in Jacksonville.

In other words, this is the quintessential sell-high, buy-low situation.

Look, I get it: New England quarterback Drake Maye (one touchdown pass, seven turnovers) has been an unmitigated disaster. At the same time, Buffalo's Josh Allen (five passing touchdowns, six rushing touchdowns) is currently — and deservedly — favored to win his second MVP in three years.

However, contrary to their perfect record, the Bills haven't been perfect in execution. In Week 1, they struggled to put away a Houston team that remains winless. In that contest, the Texans put up 31 points (they have since scored 23 in two games against Cincinnati and Indianapolis).

And while Buffalo led wire-to-wire against Detroit in Week 2, the Lions made things interesting in the second half (while scoring 31 points in the final three quarters). Then last week, following a 10-day layoff, the Bills fell behind 10-0 to a Chargers squad that lost its first two games at home to Arizona and Las Vegas.

Yes, Buffalo overcame that deficit and five turnovers — including two Allen interceptions — to post a comfortable 24-16 victory (thanks in large part to the Chargers being the Chargers). But the point is, the Bills haven't been world-beaters. 

They also didn't have an easy go of it against the Patriots last year, losing 23-20 at home (as 7.5-point favorites) and falling behind 24-7 at New England before rallying for a 35-31 win.

In fact, the Patriots are 5-1 ATS in their last six against Buffalo (all as a 'dog). And last week's ugly showing at Jacksonville aside, New England is still on a 13-4 ATS run (9-2 on the road).

Also of note: The Bills haven't covered the spread in four straight games since early in the 2021 season.

Bet: Patriots +6.5

Dolphins at Vikings (-10.5)

And now for the ultimate sell-high, buy-low scenario: The Miami Dolphins have absolutely lived down to their preseason expectations. Not only are they 0-3 SU and ATS, but all three losses were by 14-plus points.

The Dolphins are tied for dead last (with the aforementioned Patriots) in scoring offense (12 points per game). They're one of five teams allowing more than 28 points per game. And their only real asset — running back De'Von Achane — will be in street clothes the rest of the season after tearing his ACL last week against Kansas City.

Meanwhile, Miami's Week 4 opponent is 3-0 SU and ATS this season after closing out 2025 on a five-game winning streak (4-0-1 ATS).

So why am I quite possibly the only person on the planet willing to invest in the Dolphins this week? The plain and simple answer: This point spread is absurd. Because Minnesota isn't nearly as good as its untarnished record suggests.

Consider these facts: 

The Vikings got outgained 419-239 in their season-opening win over Green Bay (a game the Packers led 22-10 late in the third quarter). 

The Vikings got outgained 297-246 in their 9-3 win at Chicago in Week 2 (a game the Bears were poised to win until Caleb Williams tweaked his hamstring late).

The Vikings got outgained 243-230 (and produced just nine first downs) in last week's 23-16 win at Tampa Bay.

Out of 32 NFL teams, Minnesota ranks 32nd in total offense (238.3 ypg), 32nd in passing offense (137 ypg), 32nd in first downs (39) and 31st in third-down conversion rate.

I know the Vikings' defense has been as dominant as the offense has been inept. But this team has no business being a double-digit favorite. Against anyone. Including Miami.

Bet: Dolphins +10.5

Chiefs (-4.5) at Raiders

I was highly impressed with the Chiefs in their 31-10 season-opening beatdown of Denver. I have not been impressed — at all — since.

In the Week 2 Sunday night contest, the Colts handed Kansas City a 33-30 win, thanks to horrendous coaching decisions in overtime (and the Chiefs failed to cover as 6-point home favorites). 

Then last week, KC went to Miami, outgained the Dolphins by a whopping 5 yards (334-329) and needed 10 fourth-quarter points to turn a 14-10 nail-biter into a 24-10 victory that was far from a work of art.

As for the Raiders, I have been fully impressed — with everything — from the very first snap. And it's not just that they're another team that's 3-0 SU and ATS. It's how Las Vegas has performed across the board.

The offense has been productive (27, 26 and 35 points in victories over the Dolphins, Chargers and Saints) and efficient (only four turnovers). The defense has been stout (18 points, 316.7 yards per game), physical (10 sacks, tied for fourth most in the league) and opportunistic (nine forced turnovers). And perhaps most surprisingly, the Raiders — yes, Raiders — have been disciplined, committing just 17 penalties (tied for fifth fewest in the NFL).

Obviously, this is a huge step up in competition for a team led by 38-year-old quarterback Kirk Cousins (whose 107.2 rating is right behind the 108.9 rating of Patrick Mahomes). But I believe the new-look Silver & Black is ready to meet the challenge.

Do I expect Las Vegas to win? Tough to go there, considering it has beaten Mahomes just twice in 15 tries. But I do expect the Raiders to get inside the number — something they've done in five of their last seven games as an underdog and four of the last five times they've faced the Chiefs.

Bet: Raiders +4.5

LAST WEEK: 2-0

SEASON: 4 -4

item.title: Marcus Mariota injury update as Commanders QB exits London game
item.description: Washingon Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota exited the team's game in London against the Indianapolis Colts after suffering a knee injury on the team's second offensive series. What we know.
item.content:encoded:
Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota exited the team's game in London against the Indianapolis Colts after suffering a knee injury on the team's second offensive series.

Mariota, in his second start replacing the injured Jayden Daniels, got his right leg caught underneath a Colts lineman as he was sacked. He left with a right knee injury.

Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis has replaced Mariota at quarterback.

Marcus Mariota is heading to the medical tent after taking a hit from Laiatu Latu.
Definitely something to monitor for Washington. pic.twitter.com/vBMDxRiCTT

— Aggregate (@AggregateSports) October 4, 2026

The Commanders took an early lead after recovering a Daniel Jones fumble deep in Colts territory and converting it into a 31-yard Drew Stevens field goal.

Aided by a 35-yard run by Mariota, Washington drove down the field on its next possession before the drive stalled in the red zone. Mariota was injured on a third-down sack that preceded a 29-yard field goal from Stevens to make it 6-0.

The 32-year-old veteran walked into the locker room for tests on his right knee. He dealt with an MCL sprain on the same knee during the preseason. The Commanders listed him as questionable to return.

Kaliakmanis, a rookie out of Rutgers, was a seventh-round draft pick of the Commanders in the 2026 draft.

item.title: Week 4 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Raiders ready for their biggest game in Las Vegas vs. Chiefs
item.description: The Chiefs and Raiders are both 3-0 heading into a big AFC West game.
item.content:encoded:
When Patrick Mahomes starts at quarterback, the Kansas City Chiefs are 13-2 against the Las Vegas Raiders. But the Raiders have changed.

It's hard to get used to the idea of the Raiders being good. They've been bad for so long that it's strange to think of them any other way, unless you're still watching old clips of Ken Stabler or Marcus Allen. However, there is no evidence that their 3-0 start is fraudulent. Even if there was some trepidation about getting behind the Raiders' 2-0 start, a 35-27 comeback win at New Orleans was pretty impressive.

The Raiders are ninth in DVOA, ranking 13th in offense, ninth in defense and fifth in special teams. They're 15th in EPA per play on offense and second in EPA per play allowed. There's a new coaching staff, the roster has been remade, and the early results are impressive.

The Chiefs are good, too, of course. Any worry about Mahomes being rusty coming off ACL surgery has faded away during a 3-0 start. The Chiefs aren't going anywhere.

But this is the biggest game the Raiders have had since moving to Las Vegas. Not that the Chiefs won't be ready, but this should have a playoff feel at Allegiant Stadium. It has been a long time since the Raiders could feel this confident in what they're building. Las Vegas is a sound football team and even if they lose to a strong Chiefs team, it seems unlikely they'll be blown out. Raiders +4.5 is the pick. It's time to find out how good they might be this season.

Here are the rest of my picks against the spread for Week 4 of the NFL season:

Commanders (+3.5) over Colts

The NFL's Sunday window opens early. Set your alarm for the first 9:30 a.m. Eastern start of the year, from London. There should be plenty of scoring in this one. The Colts had the worst defense in the NFL through two weeks (though it played well last week vs. Houston) and the Commanders are 31st in the NFL in points allowed. London games are usually a bit odd, and the Commanders can score even with Marcus Mariota at QB if Jayden Daniels doesn't return. I'll take the points.

Rams (-3) over Eagles

The Eagles are 2-1, but Monday night exposed them. They were dominated by the Bears. The first two games, they barely beat Washington and Tennessee, and now those middling performances look even worse after they got blasted in Chicago. We can say the Rams are 1-2, but are probably a bad defensive pass interference call away from being 2-1 with the one loss being the weird game in Australia. I have much more faith in them than Philadelphia.

Buccaneers (+3.5) over Packers

It is frightening to pick an 0-3 Buccaneers team with an undrafted rookie quarterback. But teams this season who are starting a QB other than their Week 1 starter are 6-0 this season, according to Josh Dubow of Associated Press. And it's very hard to pick the Packers as a road favorite. They have been awful this season. Can Bucs rookie QB Jalon Daniels just do enough to keep the Bucs close? We'll find out.

Bears (-3.5) over Jets

Maybe what we saw Monday night was the typical bump a team can get from its first game with a backup quarterback. But the Bears looked good with Case Keenum, and it's fair to credit Ben Johnson's coaching for that. The Jets could be without Breece Hall, Mason Taylor and Adonai Mitchell, three key skill-position players. New York hasn't been that bad, but here's a pick for the coaching matchup.

Patriots (+6.5) over Bills

The Patriots are another team that is hard to pick. They look bad. This also feels like a playoff game for them, even though it's only Week 4. If they fall to 1-3, three games behind the Bills, the chances of winning the division get very slim. If the Patriots have any hope at all of being a factor this season, you'll see it on Sunday.

Bet the New England Patriots to cover the spread at sportsbooks right now

Jaguars (+2.5) over Bengals

It's possible Jacksonville is the team we're not talking about enough. The Jaguars had one bad half against the Broncos. In the other five halves this season, the Jaguars have outscored their three opponents 79-19. The Bengals have looked pretty good to start the season as well, though a defensive letdown last week was disappointing. We might start talking more about the Jaguars after Week 4.

Titans (+11.5) over Ravens

It's hard to come up with a logical argument for the Titans, but bad teams cover the spread often in the NFL. If you play survivor, you understand this. Also, the Ravens are coming straight off a trip to Brazil. The Titans need any edge they can get.

Texans (-2.5) over Cowboys

I refuse to give up on the Texans. It looks like they'll have Nico Collins back this week, which the offense desperately needs. Also, like the Ravens, the Cowboys are coming straight back from Brazil, and unlike Baltimore they're playing on the road. The Cowboys also had a miserable loss last week that will be hard to shake off. This is the last time we're picking Houston if it loses this week. Maybe. We'll see.

Giants (+2) over Cardinals

Arizona has been pretty good. Still, it's surprising to see the Cardinals as a road favorite. We know why. The Giants offense isn't going to be fun to watch with Jameis Winston (spoiler alert: It's unlikely to be any better with J.J. McCarthy, if and when he gets his shot). But this line seems very disrespectful to a 2-1 Giants team that will play hard and is well-coached. Also, it's a team coming from the West to play one of those early East Coast starts.

Vikings (-10.5) over Dolphins

The Dolphins will cover a spread this season. Nobody goes 0-17 against the spread. I'm not sure it's this week though. The matchup of Brian Flores' Vikings defense against a Dolphins offense now without De'Von Achane seems treacherous. If Justin Jefferson doesn't play that does give the Dolphins a shot to keep it close. But it's too hard to take Miami right now.

49ers (-2.5) over Broncos

Are the 49ers the product of an easy schedule? Perhaps to some extent. The Rams had jet lag and the Dolphins and Cardinals aren't very good. But the 49ers have handled business and Brock Purdy is red hot. They've played better than every other team so far this season. The Broncos aren't a bad team, but the first halves (they've been a no-show in the first half for all three games) is a real problem. I'll go with the NFL's hottest team and hope they take on no more injuries before kickoff.

Chargers (+7) over Seahawks

The last time Jim Harbaugh had a losing season, not counting a truncated 2020 season, was 2008 at Stanford. This season could break that streak, though. The Chargers have been legitimately awful. Even a +4 turnover margin at Buffalo didn't lead to a win, or even covering a 7-point spread. And now they get a Seattle team coming off a loss. But there's no way the Chargers can be this bad all season. Right?

Lions (-3.5) over Panthers

The Lions will score points. That seems like a safe prediction. The Panthers have played one decent offense this season and gave up 59 points to Chicago. This week they put both starting cornerbacks, Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, on injured reserve. Detroit is going to move the ball. Carolina can too. The Lions' defense is bad. But the Panthers' offensive line injuries are piling up. They're without both tackles and guard Damien Lewis is set to miss time, too, which helps the Lions. It's hard to trust Detroit's defense, but I think the Lions might score at will.

Bet the Detroit Lions to cover the spread at sportsbooks right now

Saints (-2.5) over Falcons

This isn't the best Monday night game, but it is interesting. Are the Falcons suddenly good now that they have competent quarterback play from Michael Penix Jr.? What do we make of the Saints? They are 1-2, but also won at Baltimore and nearly won at Detroit. I believe the Saints are the best team in that division, and what we saw from the Falcons in Week 3 says more about the Packers than Atlanta.

Last week: 5-11

Season to date: 20-29

item.title: NFL betting, odds, lines: Betting trends to know for Week 4's biggest games
item.description: Here are a few betting trends to help you with your wagers in Week 4.
item.content:encoded:
Three weeks into the 2026 NFL season, only five undefeated teams remain. Among that group, only three are perfect both on the field and at the betting window: the Bills, Raiders and Vikings.

Not surprisingly, Buffalo and Las Vegas are featured in this week's NFL betting trends report. So, too, are the Raiders' Week 4 opponent (fellow unbeaten Kansas City) and another squad that has yet to taste defeat (San Francisco).

What about the Vikings? Well, as a double-digit home favorite against one of four teams that is off to a 0-3 SU and ATS start, their matchup doesn't exactly qualify as "marquee."

However, the following NFL betting trends breakdown does include one squad that has yet to deliver for bettors in 2026 — a squad that has never kicked off a season 0-4 ATS.

Patriots at Bills (-6.5, 48.5)

Moneyline: Patriots +260/Bills -325

• New England got blasted 35-6 at Jacksonville in Week 3 and never threatened to cover as a 2.5-point underdog, the team's first point-spread setback this season.

That result aside, the Patriots are on regular season ATS runs of 13-4 overall, 9-2 on the road, 11-7 as an underdog, 5-1 as an underdog of more than three points and 5-1 against Buffalo (all as an underdog).

• The Bills spotted the Chargers a quick 10-0 lead in Week 3 and committed five turnovers, yet still prevailed 24-16 and covered as a seven-point home favorite.

Buffalo is off to a 3-0 start for the third consecutive year and is 3-0 ATS for the first time since covering in its first four games of 2017.

A couple of historical NFL betting trends that the Bills are facing this week: They haven't had a four-game SU and ATS winning streak since Weeks 2-5 in 2021, and they haven't started a season 4-0 SU and ATS since 1992.

• In their last five games dating to their AFC Championship Game victory at Denver, the Patriots have averaged 11.8 points. The per-game points output: 10, 13, 10, 20 and six.

Conversely, Buffalo is averaging an NFL-best 33.7 PPG this season and has tallied at least 24 points in six consecutive contests and 12 of its last 16 (playoffs included).

• Including four playoff games last year, New England is on a 6-1 under streak, with the last five in a row staying low.

Meanwhile, the over is 7-2-1 in the Bills' last 10 (postseason included).

Jaguars at Bengals (-2.5, 51.5)

Moneyline: Jaguars +125/Bengals -150

• Jacksonville and Cincinnati have started the 2026 season 2-1 SU and ATS. However, both are coming off different Week 3 results: The Jaguars throttled New England 35-6 as a 2.5-point home favorite, while the Bengals fell 30-27 at Pittsburgh as a 3.5-point road chalk.

Jacksonville is now in the midst of a 10-1 SU and ATS regular season surge. The lone blemish was a 20-13 Week 2 loss at Denver — a game the Jags led 13-3 in the second half.

On the other hand, Cincinnati hasn't won three times in a four-game stretch since closing out 2024 with five straight victories.

• During its ongoing 11-game heater, Jacksonville is 4-1 SU and ATS on the road, and 3-1 SU and ATS as an underdog.

Bet the Cincinnati Bengals to cover the spread at sportsbooks

However, when these teams met in Cincinnati in Week 2 last season, the Bengals scored a 31-27 victory as a 3.5-point home favorite. 

That extended this head-to-head NFL betting trend: Since 2020, Cincinnati is 4-0 SU and 3-1 ATS against the Jaguars. The last three meetings were decided by four, three and three points.

• After suffocating New England last week, Jacksonville's defense has now held 10 of its last 11 opponents to fewer than 21 points. During this stretch, the Jaguars are yielding an average of 13.8 PPG.

This week, they face a Cincinnati squad that is averaging 26.7 PPG through three games. The Bengals have put up at least 27 points in six of their last nine contests, dating back to Week 13 of 2025.

• The over is 7-3 in Jacksonville's last 10 road games and 3-1 in the four Jags-Bengals clashes this decade.

LA Rams (-2.5, 43.5) at Eagles

Moneyline: Rams -130/Eagles +110

• For the third time in four weeks, the Rams leave Los Angeles to face a 2025 playoff team — and they do so still searching for a positive outcome.

After kicking off 2026 with a lackluster 27-7 loss to the 49ers in Australia as a 3.5-point favorite, Los Angeles last week traveled to Denver and watched a 16-0 second-half lead evaporate into a 30-26 loss as a one-point underdog.

Including last year's postseason, the Rams 4-5 SU and 3-6 ATS over their past nine outings. All six non-covers occurred away from home.

• The Eagles traveled to Chicago as a 3.5-point favorite on Monday night and got steamrolled 27-7 by a Bears squad led by third-string quarterback Case Keenum.

Philadelphia, which also failed to cover in season-opening wins against Washington and Tennessee, is one of six teams that are 0-3 ATS. The Eagles haven't had a four-game point-spread skid since failing to cover in their final six contests of 2023. 

Then there's this eye-popping NFL betting trend: According to the SportsOddsHistory.com database that dates back to the mid-1950s, Philadelphia has never started a season 0-4 ATS.

• Going back to the start of 2024, the Eagles have won five straight games as an underdog — all away from Philly. That includes their 40-22 upset of Kansas City in Super Bowl 59.

The Eagles have been a home underdog just once since the start of 2022: In Week 13 of 2023, they lost 42-19 to the 49ers as a three-point pup.

• In Week 3 last year, the Rams traveled to Philly and fell 33-26 as a 3.5-point underdog. 

On the game's final play, L.A.'s 61-yard game-winning field goal attempt was blocked and returned for a touchdown that allowed the Eagles to cover the spread.

With that, the Rams fell to 1-9 SU and 2-8 ATS against Philadelphia since 2005.

Broncos at 49ers (-2.5, 48.5)

Moneyline: Broncos +155/49ers -130

• A week after rallying from a double-digit second-half deficit at home against Jacksonville, Denver did it again in Week 3 versus the Rams.

After surrendering the first 16 points, the Broncos outscored Los Angeles 30-10 over the final one-and-a-half quarters to win 30-26 as a one-point favorite.

Oddly, Denver's offensive production has increased by 10 points each week. They tallied 10 points in Week 1, 20 in Week 2 and 30 in Week 3.

• San Francisco is one of just five remaining undefeated teams, having taken out the Rams (27-7), Dolphins (35-13) and Cardinals (36-30).

The 49ers easily covered the point spread in its first two contests before coming up shy as a 7.5-point home favorite against Arizona in Week 3. 

As a result, San Francisco is now 8-18 ATS at home (7-16 ATS as a home favorite) since Week 8 of 2023 (postseason included).

• Since starting 0-2 in 2024, Denver is 26-9 SU in the regular season — but only 9-8 in true road games. What's more, the Broncos have failed to cover in four straight as a visitor (although they were favored three times).

On the bright side, Denver won its last four games as an underdog in 2025. That streak ended with a 31-10 season-opening loss at Kansas City as a 1.5-point pup. 

• The over is 20-11 in the Niners' last 31 games at Levi's Stadium, with 18 contests clearing 46 combined points.

Conversely, four of Denver's last five regular season games have stayed low. Only Sunday night's contest against the Rams topped 41 points.

Chiefs (-4.5, 47.5) at Raiders

Moneyline: Chiefs -225/Raiders +185

• Kansas City has followed last year's 0-6 season-ending slump with a 3-0 start to 2026.

In Week 3, the Chiefs went to Miami and scored a comfortable 24-10 win as a 9.5-point road chalk.

Kansas City started 4-0 or better in four consecutive seasons from 2017-2020. Since then, it's only happened once: The 2024 Chiefs opened with a nine-game winning streak.

• The Raiders continued their stunning start to the season with a 35-27 comeback win at New Orleans as a four-point underdog. Las Vegas trailed 27-16 late in the third quarter before rallying with 19 unanswered points.

The Raiders, who have already matched their victory total from last season, are 3-0 SU for the first time since 2021 and 3-0 ATS for the first time since 2013.

The last time the Silver & Black opened a season with a four-game SU and ATS winning streak: 2002, the last time the franchise reached the Super Bowl.

• Las Vegas capped 2025 with a 14-12 victory over Kansas City as a 3.5-point underdog, then kicked off this season with a 27-13 rout of Miami as a 3.5-point home favorite.

Prior to those two contests, though, the Raiders had lost 12 of 14 games at Allegiant Stadium (5-8-1 ATS).

One positive NFL betting trend working in Las Vegas' favor: It is 5-2 ATS in its last seven as an underdog.

Bet the Kansas City Chiefs to cover the spread at sportsbooks

• Since 2013, Kansas City is 21-5 SU in this bitter AFC West rivalry, including 10-3 SU away from home.

In fact, the Chiefs had won seven consecutive road games against the Raiders until losing last year's season finale — a game quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) missed. 

With Mahomes on the field, the Chiefs are 13-2 against the Raiders, including 7-0 on the road. However, K.C. is only 8-7 ATS overall and 4-3 ATS on the road in those games.

• The under is 20-5 in the Chiefs' last 25 games (9-2 on the road). Only six of those 25 games hurdled 47 combined points.

Relatedly, 20 of the Raiders' last 26 contests have fallen short of 48 points.

item.title: Arrowhead Pride readers’ 2026 Hot Seat watch for NFL coaches
item.description: Which NFL Head Coach will be the first to go this season?
item.content:encoded:
They say the NFL stands for the Not For Long league, and nothing is truer than when you’re talking about head coaching positions. In a world ruled by “what have you done for me lately” and teams owned by billionaires who are used to getting their way and want to win now, it seems every coaching position in the NFL comes with an expiration date.

In a league that has 32 teams, 37 NFL head coaches have been fired over the last five seasons. That’s an average of 7.4 coaches getting the axe each year. And while some franchises are perennial residents on the list of teams searching for the right person to lead, it’s interesting to think that, aside from a handful of exceptions like the Chiefs, the league essentially refreshes every five seasons.

Still, no man is immune from the hot seat. It doesn’t matter if you’re former New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick; if you don’t have enough W’s in the win column, your tushy is getting toasty.

Fans have always been vocal about which coaches should consider putting their homes on the market, so we asked you, the readers over on The Feed, who you think should be on the hot seat in 2026.

Based on your feedback, we narrowed it down to five NFL head coaches most in danger of losing their jobs this season.

Here is what you said.

1. Todd Bowles – Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Heat Rating: Using a blow torch to build a homemade rocket chair, and realizing too late that you installed it backward

Pretty much a unanimous selection by the AP Readers. Bowles’ time in Tampa may be coming to an end after a 0-3 start. But despite being winless, the Buccaneers play in a terrible division and are only one game out of first place, and it’s still early, so if they can turn things around, they might still be gifted a playoff berth. My bet, though, is that the slide continues and he doesn’t finish the season as Tampa’s head coach.

Here is what you had to say:

“Todd Bowles. He cashed in all his chips when he fired all the coordinators. That move saddled him with all the blame. Now the Buccaneers, who are a semi-talented roster, are 0-3 with an ugly loss to the Browns. No one to blame it on except Bowles, who also turned last years team from an early season contender to sitting at home in January”

– ChiefoftheWest111

“Bowles… Never pay Baker a compensated Baker is a losing Baker.”

– Just a guy

“Todd Bowles. Again, he might be paying the price for a flawed roster under-going a soft rebuild. Even so, Bowles entered the season on a warm seat. If the team keeps losing, I could see management making a change to see if it could spark a run to the top of a bad division.”

– ChiefZed

2. Matt LaFleur – Green Bay Packers

Heat Rating: 1980s-era metal playground slide in the middle of July while wearing Daisy Dukes

The Packers went all in last season when they acquired edge rusher Micah Parsons from the Dallas Cowboys. Unfortunately, things haven’t panned out as they planned. Green Bay finished just 9-7 last year and are off to a 1-2 start so far in 2026. The Packers haven’t won their division since 2021, and may decide, much like the Baltimore Ravens did last season, that they need to make a change to get over the hump, or to lead them in a full roster rebuild.

Here is what you had to say:

“The Packers woes go back to the end of last year.. Not sure why they extended LaFleur after the way things ended for them.”

– krav_nazt

“What’s interesting about the Packers: apparently in the last 4 years they’ve only made the playoffs as a 7th seed 3 of those years. So one could argie had they not extended that 7th seed he’d be riding multiple seasons without a playoff berth”

– Andyreidsmustache

“Matt Lefleur(I think he has lost the room)”

– Swaf

3. Jim Harbaugh – Los Angeles Chargers

Heat Rating: SUV seat warmer with a faulty wire that slowly keeps getting hotter and hotter until you suddenly realize there is a hole in the backside of your Zubaz

You almost have to feel bad for Chargers fans. First, their team moved to LA, where they are the equivalent of Dewey Cox in his father’s eyes. Then they get their hopes up when they sign Harbaugh as head coach, thinking they are getting the guy who won the National Championship at the University of Michigan. Instead, they got a snake oil salesman adept at slipping town just before things fall apart. This time, though, the timeline might have caught up with him.

Here is what you had to say:

“If the Chargers are winless going into their bye, somebody is getting fired.”

– AZDiamond75


“The NFL averages something like 5 HC turnovers per year. After 3 weeks, when comparing preseason expectations vs early results, you’d put Jim Harbaugh…”

– houjix

“After the way the Chargers have looked early I will start with Harbaugh.”

– chiefhawk

item.title: 5 things to watch as Giants face Cardinals in Week 4 of 2026 NFL season
item.description: The Giants face the Cardinals on Sunday at MetLife Stadium in Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
Despite Jaxson Dart and Brian Burnsboth being out for the season, the Giants still have a chance to sit atop the NFC East after this weekend. If they can beat the 1-2 Arizona Cardinals and the struggling Philadelphia Eagles lose to the Los Angeles Rams, New York will be 3-1 and in sole possession of first place.

Let’s review the top storylines to watch as the Giants look to keep the momentum going...

Can Jameis Winston step up with J.J. McCarthy waiting in the wings?

After Dart’s season-ending injury early in Week 2, Winston has stepped in at quarterback, but he’s struggled so far. He completed just 11 of 27 passes against the Rams and only passed for 118 yards in the win over the Tennessee Titans.

Although New York traded for McCarthy during the week, the intention is not to make the 2024 top 10 pick an immediate starter. However, with a more established challenger to his status as the current starter, the pressure is on Winston to be better this week. 

More likely to break out: Malik Nabers or Marvin Harrison Jr.?

Nabers and Harrison have both been struggling this season, but each is capable of a breakout game, which could make the difference on Sunday.

Harrison, whose numbers and consistency dropped off last season, got off to a bad start this year, as he only caught one pass in the first two games. However, he had three catches for 40 yards on Sunday, which is a step in the right direction and could signify that he’s ready for a bigger role in the Cardinals’ offense. A game against the Giants’ struggling cornerbacks could be just what he needs.

Like Harrison, Nabers also had a good rookie season, but it’s been injuries rather than inconsistent play that have affected him since then. While already playing on a surgically repaired knee, Nabers also had a shoulder injury and, as a result, he has just 28 yards on six catches over the past two games. The Giants desperately need him to boost their struggling offense, which is 0-for-4 in the red zone over the past two weeks.

Can New York stop Jeremiyah Love?

This year’s third overall pick, Love is trending in the right direction for the Cardinals.

After being held to 70 yards on 20 carries in the first two games, Love racked up 109 yards from scrimmage on Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers as he averaged 4.3 yards per carry and caught five passes.

New York’s 12th-ranked run defense hasn’t given up a 100-yard rusher this season, and Love may make a bid to be the first.

Is Arvell Reese up to the task of covering Trey McBride?

Arizona’s best offensive weapon is McBride, who set the all-time single-season receptions record for tight ends last season with 126 catches. He’s been just as productive so far this season, with his 26 receptions in the first three games just one shy of the league lead for all players.

In coverage, Arizona may look for opportunities to isolate McBride against Reese, whose coverage deficiencies have been exposed at times this season.

Reese is coming off his best game as a pro, as he had 13 tackles, a tackle for loss, and a pass breakup in Sunday’s 12-7 win against the Titans. He could gain some more confidence if he emerges from this weekend’s challenge with his reputation intact.

Will John Harbaugh’s experience prove crucial against first-year head coach Mike LaFleur?

Harbaugh overcame all the injury issues as he led his team to the win over Tennessee on Sunday. If he can continue to overcome the adversity and win this weekend, that should ensure the Giants will still be in the mix at the bye week, when they’ll have more of a chance to regroup.

On Sunday, Harbaugh faces LaFleur, whose team surprised many analysts with an impressive Week 1 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. However, since then, they were blown out by Seattle before dropping to 1-2 with a 36-30 loss to the 49ers.

This is the sort of game where you would expect the Giants to have a coaching advantage. Harbaugh’s years of experience should give them confidence down the stretch if it’s a close game.

It’s worth noting, however, that LaFleur had been working with Sean McVay on the Rams’ staff for the past three seasons. He may therefore opt for a gameplan that has similarities to the one the Rams used to blow out New York two weeks ago.

item.title: Joey Porter Jr. expected to play for Cowboys in Week 4 after missing start of season with back injury
item.description: Joey Porter Jr. is feeling better after a mid-week trade to the Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is healed. After missing the start of the season due to a back injury, Porter is expected to play in Week 4 after being traded to the Cowboys, according to ESPN.

Porter, however, is expected to have his snaps limited during the contest.

Joey Porter Jr. is set to play for the Dallas Cowboys days after being traded from Pittsburgh, but the team is expected to limit his snaps vs Houston.

One source estimated about 30 snaps or so, depending on the flow of the game.

— Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) October 4, 2026

It will mark the first game all season in which Porter has played. The 26-year-old missed the first three weeks of the regular season due to both back and conditioning issues. Despite being able to put in work during practices, Porter was constantly ruled out on game days by the Pittsburgh Steelers after missing time in the offseason due to a contract dispute.

That dispute ultimately resulted in the Steelers trading Porter to the Cowboys on Wednesday. The Cowboys sent a sixth-round pick and a second-round pick to the Steelers as part of the deal.

Following the trade, Porter was not listed among the Cowboys' injuries and received no injury designation on the team's final report, suggesting he would suit up in Week 4 against the Houston Texans.

While there's an uncharitable read on the situation that suggests Porter was never truly hurt and was sitting out over his contract situation in Pittsburgh, the limited snap count for Porter in Week 4 does suggest there are legitimate concerns about immediately throwing him into a game.

Porter, who is in the final year of his rookie contract, was at odds with the Steelers all offseason over a contract extension. There was a hard deadline on a deal getting done, as the Steelers — generally — do not negotiate contracts during the season. That deadline passed without a deal, putting Porter and the team at an impasse.

That impasse was solved with Wednesday's trade. Though he still doesn't have a contract extension, Porter will reportedly take the field for the Cowboys in Week 4. If he can go out and turn in a strong season, Porter should eventually get the mega-contract he's seeking, whether from the Cowboys or from another franchise once he hits the free-agent market.

item.title: Slim majority in Broncos Country believes late-game heroics are sustainable
item.description: When the Broncos step onto the field at Levi’s Stadium this afternoon to take on the undefeated 49ers, only a slim majority of Denver fans believe the team can mount a comeback if it comes to that. After two weeks of thrilling victories thanks to come-from-behind, fourth-quarter comebacks (the best kind of wins, tbh), there […]
item.content:encoded:
When the Broncos step onto the field at Levi’s Stadium this afternoon to take on the undefeated 49ers, only a slim majority of Denver fans believe the team can mount a comeback if it comes to that.

After two weeks of thrilling victories thanks to come-from-behind, fourth-quarter comebacks (the best kind of wins, tbh), there is doubt within Broncos Country that such heroic tactics are sustainable.

But you know who does believe it?

Head coach Sean Payton, and more importantly, quarterback Bo Nix.

That doesn’t mean the coach or team is gaming for second-half surges, but hero-like comebacks aren’t a problem either.

“Honestly, I think the huddle’s calm. We just have a very calm huddle. Smooth in and out, we don’t panic. Nobody really has to say much, but we’re all just motivating each other and encouraging each other,” Nix said earlier this week. “I think once you do it a few times, you just know you can do it. …At the end of the day, it’s just doing it over and over and knowing I have the guys to go out there and go on a game-winning drive because we’ve done it against many, many good teams.”

The Broncos are currently last in the NFL for first-half scoring, and Payton would definitely like to change that.

“We certainly recognize it’s not good, but that has to improve and it’s not just me up here talking,” Payton said of the slow starts so far this season. “When I go through the PowerPoints right now, the Week 3 rankings, we don’t even look at. We just recognize it isn’t good. It has to improve.”

The good news is that Payton’s record in October is historically very good.

In fact, his .761 winning percentage during October is the best in NFL history among guys who coached at least 50 games in the month. And he let the team know it, emphasizing why his teams have played winning football in October.

“As we called everyone up [in the huddle, the message] was, ‘October was good for us a year ago, and that’s because you guys made it a priority during the week,'” Payton said Wednesday. “It was kind of back to that. We’re early in this race. We have to be finding these areas that don’t become another mistake [in] Week 5 or Week 6.”

The Niners will be a huge test of that progress during the week.

item.title: Defensive head-to-head preview: Saints vs Falcons
item.description: Saints vs Falcons matchup in the 20th anniversary of the Domecoming game and the Saints defense has to bring pressure
item.content:encoded:
The New Orleans Saints are getting ready for their only primetime matchup of the season when the Atlanta Falcons come to the Superdome on Monday night. The Falcons are hoping to have found some consistency at the QB position with the return of Michael Penix Jr. for what will be his second start of the season. The defense for the Falcons has been pretty good so far. Through the first three games, they are 8th overall in total defense, compared to the Saints, who are 20th.

The Falcons currently have the best rushing defense in the NFL. They are allowing an average of only 47.7 rushing yards per game through three games. That is not something the Saints need to be matching up against this week, considering the loss of Travis Etienne Jr., who was recently placed on IR with a hamstring injury. The Saints’ rushing attack was already having trouble getting into a rhythm, and now, with the best run defense in the league coming into town, it will only add more to Tyler Shough’s plate.

Jeff Ulbrich is the defensive coordinator for the Falcons, and this is his second season serving as the defensive play-caller. Ulbrich utilizes multiple fronts for his defense and does not rely on a traditional three- or four-man front. The Falcons’ defense does not blitz often but will attempt to disguise its coverage from pre-snap to post-snap looks. So far this year, that has not worked too well against the pass. The Falcons currently have the 29th-ranked pass defense in the league.

The loss of A.J. Terrell, who is currently on IR, and Kaden Elliss, who is now leading the Saints’ defense, has absolutely affected the outlook of this Falcons pass defense. Terrell is one of the best corners in the league, and Elliss was a versatile linebacker who was able to rush the passer and cover when needed. Not to mention the losses of others like Dee Alford, James Pearce Jr. and David Onyemata. That’s a lot of vital reps to replace from players who had a major impact on the Falcons’ pass defense. While the Saints’ rushing offense may be struggling, Shough and Olave have to be salivating at the opportunity to play against such a beleaguered Falcons secondary and pass defense. Olave is currently ranked in the top five across several categories in the NFL so far this season. This will be a great opportunity for him to have another major impact game.

As for the Saints, the defense has not been building off the strong end to the season it had last year. So far, the Saints rank 20th in total defense. The matchup to be concerned about will be the Saints’ run defense against the Falcons’ rushing offense. The Falcons and Bijan Robinson are coming off a game in which their star back ran for almost 200 yards against the Packers, so his confidence is high.

The only thing that should give him pause is that Brandon Staley and the Saints had him figured out last year. Robinson totaled only 103 yards on 29 carries in two games against the Saints last season. So, the Saints will have to make stopping Robinson the priority. This will force the Falcons into third-and-long situations, where Atlanta has struggled. The Falcons are 12-of-35 on third down for a 34.3% conversion rate this season. The Saints, on the other hand, have allowed opposing offenses to convert at a 47.1% rate. Something will have to give.

Last week, the Falcons found a third-down groove against the Packers, converting 60% of their opportunities by going 6-of-10. The question becomes: Was that an exception, or was it the result of having a better QB playing since Penix was able to return last week?

The Saints’ pass defense has been solid. The Saints currently rank 16th, which is literally in the middle of the league. This game will be like playing the Lions and the Raiders: They have to get pressure on Penix and get him off his timing. This would be a great game for Cam Jordan to tap into the fountain of youth. Jordan loves playing against the Falcons, and over his career, he has recorded 26 sacks against the Dirty Birds.

The Saints, as a defense, have seven sacks so far this season, with Chase Young accounting for half of those with 3.5 through three games. If the Saints can stop the run and generate a consistent pass rush, they will be able to put the offense in a better position to take advantage of a very weak Falcons pass defense.

Not to mention, this will be the 20th anniversary of the Domecoming game, and the crowd will be electric. The defense needs to feed off that energy and really elevate its play on Monday night.

[…]
item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers could be without quarterback Baker Mayfield longer than initially anticipated.

According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Mayfield is expected to miss somewhere between three and six weeks with the dislocated right thumb he suffered against the Minnesota Vikings, with his return ultimately hinging on when he can comfortably grip a football again.

The good news for Mayfield and the Buccaneers is that an MRI revealed no fracture and no damage to the ligaments or tendons in his throwing hand. Tampa Bay has also avoided placing Mayfield on injured reserve for now, leaving the door open for him to return toward the shorter end of the recovery timetable.

Head coach Todd Bowles originally said Mayfield would miss a minimum of three weeks following the injury. That would keep him sidelined against the Green Bay Packers, Dallas Cowboys and Pittsburgh Steelers before potentially returning against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7.

However, Mayfield’s ability to regain his grip strength will ultimately dictate when he gets back on the field. Tampa Bay will not want to rush its starting quarterback back before he can properly control the football and make throws with his usual accuracy and velocity.

In the meantime, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will take over under center, beginning with Sunday’s home matchup against Green Bay.

item.title: NFL will surely want to plug "hold-in" loophole, but it won't be easy
item.description: When the workers find real power, management can't take it.
item.content:encoded:
When the workers find real power, management can't take it.

Under the NFL's Collective Bargaining Agreement, the workers have found real power. In one very specific way.

The 2020 CBA made it much more difficult for players to hold out. Enter the hold-in.

In many cases, the team allows a player who wants a new contract to not practice while talks continue. The player is in the building (once a player reports it's difficult under the CBA to leave), he's working out, he's attending meetings. It's just a matter of time before a deal is done.

Unless a deal isn't done. And if the player is willing to cite an injury, embellished or flat-out fabricated, to refuse to provide services until the player gets what he wants, the team is stuck.

Last year, the Cowboys cried "uncle" after they realized that their apparent plan to kick the can on the Micah Parsons contract through the 2025 season wasn't going to work, because Parsons wasn't going to play, due to a back injury. This year, former Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. cited a back injury (which has suddenly healed, to no surprise) to sit out all of training camp, all of the preseason, and the first three games of the regular season. On Wednesday, the Steelers threw in the towel and traded Porter to, coincidentally, the Cowboys.

The powers-that-be won't like this trend, because the players have found a way to crack the code on the CBA. After years of playing football, any player could point to one or more body parts that create chronic pain and/or present a risk of more significant injury.

If a player is committed to the approach, what can the team do? Tell him they don't believe him? Fine him? Suspend him?

It would spark a legal mess under the CBA, a P.R. debacle for the team, and a potential morale issue in the locker room.

Enter the looming talks on a new labor deal. Surely, the Management Council is already brainstorming strategies to end the hold-in.

One fairly simple possibility would entail arranging for a neutral, third-party doctor to examine the player and to determine whether he has an injury and, if so, whether he shouldn't be practicing or playing because of it. If the doctor says the player is fine, and if the player persists in refusing to practice or play, the player becomes susceptible to an immediate fine, or a suspension.

Still, that's far easier said than done. Most competent doctors will tell patients that they know their bodies better than anyone. Most competent doctors aren't in the habit of telling patients they're faking a condition.

Really, who wants to be potentially responsible for informing a player he doesn't have a real injury and essentially forcing him to play when he doesn't want to?

The better approach could be to financially incentivize the player to practice and play. Over the past 20 years or so, offseason workout bonuses and per-game active roster bonuses have become an effective tool to tie pay to actual performance. A significant training-camp (and/or regular-season) practice participation bonus would raise the stakes for players who can't (or won't) suit up. Per-game active roster bonuses, which currently aren't part of the standard rookie deals, could be added to the formula for paying draft picks.

Obviously, this would punish players who are legitimately injured, and it would tempt some players to risk further injury in the name of earning their pay. But the teams already employ that approach with active-roster bonuses in veteran contracts. For young players, it becomes an important device to avoid a hold-in after their third seasons, when they become eligible for second contracts.

The problem is that the goalposts will potentially move. A player who wants a new contract and who previously would have cited an injury to avoid playing could just half-ass it through practices or games. But it's one thing to refuse to play; it's another to put on the uniform, step into the arena, and constantly make business decisions. That would open the player up to fair criticism from media and fans, and to resentment from his teammates.

Still, management has to be miffed that players have found a way to stage what is essentially a one-man wildcat strike until he gets what he wants. And it would be foolish to think the league isn't already trying to come up with a way to end it.

That said, some owners may not mind it. In 2025, the Cowboys' loss was Green Bay's gain, after the Packers traded for Parsons. In 2026, the Cowboys benefited from the tactic that was used against them last year, with the trade that brought Porter to Dallas.

Given that all owners could have their contractual rights to a player short-circuited by a conscious refusal to practice or play based on a non-existent injury, the overall balance likely tips in favor of trying to find a way to claw back the power the players have created by claiming, in an industry rife with injuries, that they aren't healthy enough to work — even if they are.

item.title: Eagles make change at QB2 against the Rams
item.description: After a tough Week 3 loss, the Eagles are turning back to Tanner McKee as the backup quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles have hesitated to name a firm backup quarterback through three games this season, and neither Tanner McKee or Andy Dalton did much to earn the spot through the preseason. Still, the team went with Dalton as QB2 for the first three games, and then in Week 3 against the Bears, he had to take the field as Jalen Hurts was evaluated for a concussion. Three plays later, the soon-to-be 39-year-old veteran threw an interception right to a rookie Bears safety in the back of the end zone.

Head coach Nick Sirianni was asked this week if the interception would affect who the backup would be against the Rams in Week 4, and, as usual, he was reluctant to name anyone. Despite not publicly shaming Dalton for the turnover, we learned on Sunday morning that the Eagles are planning to promote Tanner McKee back to QB2 — a spot he’s held the past couple seasons.

Hopefully, the Eagles don’t need to rely on McKee or Dalton against the Rams, and Hurts is able to stay healthy throughout the game.

item.title: Eagles News: Saquon Barkley is in an unprecedented fantasy football slump
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 10/4/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

Saquon Barkley’s lack of produciton isn’t even his fault; he’s looked pretty spry out there. He’s had big games against the Los Angeles Rams before, so, maybe he can deliver a big game on the ground here? The Eagles could certainy use that from him with DeVonta Smith out.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

NFL Week 4 preview: Picks, predictions, schedule, betting odds, fantasy tips – ESPN

Fantasy nugget: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley has been held under 10 fantasy points in three consecutive games for the first time in his career. He also has yet to surpass 15 rushing attempts in a game. The Rams’ defensive front ranks eighth in run stop win rate, so this could be another tough matchup for the Eagles’ offensive line and running game.

Rams’ keys to victory: Slow Saquon – Turf Show Times

Defensive Key: Slow Saquon Barkley. With the Philadelphia Eagles being without DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert, the Eagles offense will feature three skill players: Saquon Barkley, Dontayvion Wicks, and Makai Lemon. Barkley is clearly the more talented of the three. Expect the Eagles to feed Barkley as many touches as possible to limit Hurts from having to drop back all game long. While Jalen Hurts is a threat to run with his legs; slowing Barkley is the first key in the defense being able to get off the grass.

Eagles Film Preview: Scheme will have to help this team beat the Rams – BGN

The Rams have been a very good pass defense through three weeks, but injuries in the secondary could give the Eagles opportunities this Sunday. Of course, the Eagles have their own injury problems, particularly at receiver, so this matchup is difficult to pin down. I like parts of the Rams’ defense a lot. I also think the Eagles have to find ways to attack it, because I have no interest in watching this offense spend another afternoon hoping the defense will win the game for them. It won’t happen this week!

The Eagles can survive this tough stretch, as long as Nick Sirianni doesn’t let them fall apart – Inquirer

The good thing for Sirianni and his team this time is that the standard for success has to be different, has to be a little lower. Losses to the Rams and to the Jaguars wouldn’t necessarily be the worst possible outcomes for them. The nature of those losses — of how the Eagles play — would matter more. Put simply, even if they go down, the Eagles have to go down fighting. They can’t get blown out again. They have to remain competitive. They have to give everyone, themselves included, reason to believe they can turn things around once they get healthier, once all their defensive starters settle into Vic Fangio’s system, once Mannion has more opportunities to show whether he’s the budding genius the Eagles have billed him to be.

Will the Eagles’ defense ever make another big play? – NBCSP

It’s been 265 days since they intercepted a pass. It’s been 279 days since they recovered an opponent’s fumble or got two sacks in a game from their edge rushers. Big defensive plays have been few and far between for the Eagles so far this year, and they could sure use some Sunday afternoon when they host the Rams at the Linc. “Obviously, you want to get those big plays,” Cooper DeJean said. “But I think over time, those things will come. I mean, we’re three games into the season. I think once one comes, they’ll come in bunches.” The Eagles are the only NFL team without a takeaway so far and only the 15th team ever with no takeaways through three games. Only two of the first 14 made the playoffs – the 1979 Broncos and 2004 Rams. The Eagles are also tied for 28th – with the Rams – with just three sacks. Only the Cowboys (2), Giants (1) and Dolphins (0) have fewer.

Detroit Lions elevate DB for Panthers game – Pride Of Detroit

The Detroit Lions announced on Saturday that they have elevated safety Jalen Mills for their Sunday night game against the Carolina Panthers in Week 4. This is the second straight week Mills has been called up from the practice squad as the Lions navigate a bunch of injuries at safety. Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph remain on the physically unable to perform list, while Avonte Maddox and Thomas Harper landed on injured reserve this past week. The good news for the Lions is that Branch’s return seems imminent.

Patriots elevate veteran defensive backs Kindle Vildor, Mike Brown from practice squad for Week 4 – Pats Pulpit

Vildor, 29, picked off one pass during his preseason audition in Foxborough and joined the initial practice squad after being released as a vested vet at the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline. The 5-foot-11, 189-pound cornerback out of Georgia Southern originally entered the league with the Chicago Bears in the fifth round of the 2020 draft at No. 163 overall. Stops with the Tennessee Titans, Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions and Tampa Bay Buccaneers were logged before signing a one-year deal with the Patriots as an unrestricted free agent in March. Standing 80 games, including 27 starts, into his career, Vildor has had a hand in 140 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and two interceptions. His career spans 2,105 snaps on defense and 573 snaps on special teams.

Seahawks sign Velus Jones Jr off practice squad, elevate Trevon Diggs for first time – Field Gulls

Meanwhile, the Seahawks elevated veteran cornerback Trevon Diggs and [former Eagles] safety Maxen Hook from the practice squad. Diggs signed with Seattle during preseason and recorded an interception in his lone August appearance against the Kansas City Chiefs. item.title: Browns Week 4 lookback: Resiliency, defensive masterclass, offense physicality
item.description: Believe it or not, the Cleveland Browns are 3-1 and fans get to enjoy while Week 4 finishes off. A few lookbacks
item.content:encoded:
Before the season, if anyone was to tell you that the Cleveland Browns would be 3-1 four weeks into a season in which the team is supposed to be rebuilding, would you have believed them? If not, understandable. Even more so after the team’s Week 1 loss. Run back and tell your past self: the Cleveland Browns are 3-1 after their Thursday night statement win over hated divisional rival the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Out of the three victories this year, this one felt different. In a good way.

1st Down: Resilient mind, resilient team

As mentioned on the Amazon Prime broadcast by commentator Ryan Fitzpatrick, the resiliency from this Browns team is something that cannot be ignored. Dominant 1st half (after a slow start), but a slow 2nd half in which the Steelers looked to capture some momentum, but instead of finding a way to lose, the team found a way to win.

Cleveland continued to fight, and in the end they found a way to win. The one thing that you can’t measure when it comes to a young team is grit. The Browns have that, and they showcased it on Thursday night in front of a national audience.

2nd Down: Defensive masterclass on display

I am chalking the defensive performance that the Browns had in Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars as an outlier. So far, the defense might be even better than it was last year. Granted, it’s early, but the Cleveland defense was making life miserable for Pittsburgh.

Cornerback Denzel Ward getting his just attention nationally is well deserved. Ward is a top five cornerback in this league, and the Browns are fortunate to have him

The defensive line was causing consistent pressure, linebackers were flowing and making plays, and the secondary made plays when called upon. I reiterated how much of an upgrade defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg was over Jim Schwartz because of how he can make this defense evolve without changing the main thing that makes them really good. Play man coverage, rush four, bring a creative blitz, and it worked.

The team only gave up a couple explosive plays during a really stout performance for the defense.

3rd Down: Offense steps up, physicality was shown

Two things. Say what you want about the Browns and their offense, but they are starting to gel. Quarterback Deshaun Watson played well once again yesterday, even if not perfect. He played well in the 1st half; 2nd half wasn’t as stout, but when he was required to make a play, he came through when called upon. Cleveland fans have yearned for competent quarterback play, and the team is getting it.

The Browns offensive line was far from perfect, but center Luke Wypler deserves a ton of credit for his performance. When called upon after Elgton Jenkins was ruled out with a concussion, Wypler made his presence known.

Lost in the win, the one thing that stood out to me was how Cleveland imposed their will on the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Browns controlled the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball; the team felt faster and looser. The team made it a point to be the aggressors, and they did for the majority of the game.

4th Down: Yeah they are 3-1 but…

This isn’t meant to be negative, but it’s more of a reality. Yes, the Cleveland Browns are 3-1, and it’s great. However, the team cannot continue to win games in the way that they are winning. Allow me to explain. It’s fun that the Browns are winning. However, the constant mistakes and penalties will come back to bite them when they go up against a better team. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are somewhat of a mess, the Carolina Panthers are a question mark, and the Pittsburgh Steelers are not as good as people may think. Yet, Cleveland won all of those games against those teams.

They found a way to overcome their mistakes, but they need to understand how to string together a complete game from both sides of the ball with minimal mistakes. If the team can do that, then the possibilities are endless.

Extra Points

  • The Pittsburgh Steelers aren’t a good team and Thursday night showed how flawed they are. The team looks older, slower and overall just a worse version of last year’s team.
  • Staying with the Steelers, I’m willing to say something that no one else will. The Browns have already surpassed the Steelers in terms of roster building/outlook. Cleveland has young ascending talent that Pittsburgh lacks because they traded those players away. It feels as if the Steelers have no plan but the Browns do.
  • Some of the penalties were unnecessary; other penalties had me giving a side eye toward the refs
  • Unfortunately, the Browns don’t have another primetime game this season; I feel it would be beneficial if the country sees more of Cleveland. Thankfully, or not, the flex schedule could change that sooner than later
  • The Cleveland Browns are 3-1. I am surprised, like everyone, that this is real and amazing.

What are some of your takeaways now that you’ve had a few days to process?
