item.title: Week 4 NFL Survivor strategy and picks with safe, value, and trap picks
item.description: David Fucillo provides NFL Survivor pool tips in Week 4, offering up safe, value, and trap picks.
item.content:encoded:
October is upon us! The NFL heads into Week 4 and with the fall weather, football really and truly is in the air!

Last week opened with the Falcons thumping the Packers in Green Bay, which tells us plenty about how bad the Packers are right now. The most notable upset has to be the Marcus Mariota-led Commanders beating the previously unbeaten Seahawks, but the Jaguars crushing the Patriots was also a bit of a surprise.

I’m back with my week 4 Survivor picks ahead of Steelers-Browns on Thursday Night Football. Survivor involves picking one team each week to win. If they win you advance, if they lose you’re out in most cases. I’m in one pool with four entries, but it’s also a double-elimination pool. One of my entries was out in two weeks thanks to the Chargers and Bucs losing the first two weeks of the season. Another entry was Steelers in Week 1 and then Bucs in Week 2, so I was down to one strike there. I made three picks last week, with two 49ers and one Chiefs pick moving me on for another week.

Below I’ve got a look at the safest choices, best value picks, and then trap picks. I’ll post my own picks at the end. I’ll update on Sunday once I lock in my three picks for the weekend.

I’ve included odds for the favorite in each game, courtesy of FanDuel.

Safest picks

Vikings (-10.5) over Dolphins
Ravens (-11.5) over Titans

We have two double digit favorites this week and both are the safe plays. The Vikings are the better play this weekend because there are not many options left to use them. They’re projected favorites at home against the Falcons and Panthers in Week 12 and Week 13, but if you haven’t used them yet, the Jaguars at home against the Titans and the Broncos at home against the Dolphins will be better values.

Best value picks

Vikings (-10.5) over Dolphins

Minnesota really is the value play this week. A lot of folks will use the Ravens, but the Vikings are the one that make the most sense across the board.

Trap pick

Seahawks (-7) over Chargers
Bills (-6.5) over Patriots

Seattle should be able to bounce back after their struggles in Washington, while LA has been a disaster. I’m not ready to give up on the Chargers, and this is a dangerous game for the Seahawks.

I think the Bills probably roll the Patriots, but there’s no reason to make a divisional pick at this stage of your contests.

My picks this week

I don’t like putting all my eggs in one basket, but the Vikings are a tempting basket. I’ll probably use the Ravens for one pick and the Vikings for two, but I’m going to sleep on it the next few days.

Sunday update: I decided to go with two Vikings picks and one Ravens pick. Notably, I went with the Vikings in my pool where I’m down one strike already. I split Vikings and Ravens for my two entries with no strikes.

item.title: Chicago Bears expected to start inexperienced QB - Can New York Jets take advantage?
item.description: The Jets may have an opportunity to exploit a Bears QB’s inexperience this week
item.content:encoded:
As far as I am aware, as of the time of writing this article, the Chicago Bears had made no official announcement regarding who will start for them at quarterback in place of the injured Caleb Williams. Nonetheless, rumors inevitably leak out, and the word out of Chicago is that 26 year old Tyson Bagent will start the game at quarterback for the Bears.

Is this a mistake by Chicago? Last week Bagent was unavailable due to his own injury issues, and 38 year old Case Keenum came off the bench for his first NFL start in almost three years. It went swimmingly. Keenum turned back the clock as he completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards, two touchdowns and no turnovers. He posted a passer rating of 111 on the way to a dominant 27 – 7 Bears win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Keenum kept the offense moving with an outstanding mix of short passes as he got the ball out quickly and decisively. His reward for this performance is a place on the bench against the Jets.

Tyson Bagent will take the reins today for the Bears. Like Keenum prior to last week, Bagent hasn’t started an NFL game since 2023. That was Bagent’s rookie year. As an undrafted free agent that year out of tiny Shepherd University, Bagent was ill-prepared to be thrust into a starting role so soon, and it showed. In four starts in 2023 Tyson Bagent threw for just 776 yards, an average of just 194 per game. He threw just three touchdown passes while racking up six interceptions in 2023, an unfortunate 1:2 ratio. Bagent had a very bad 6.0 yards per pass attempt and 71 passer rating. It was about what you’d expect for the inexperienced passer.

Bagent hasn’t started a game in the NFL since his rookie year. He has thrown just 15 NFL passes since then. Has he significantly developed in the interim? Is he much better prepared to face NFL defenses with a couple of years under his belt? Who knows? Bagent has had some success in preseason games, but preseason action is no substitute for the real thing.

Case Keenum has always been the NFL equivalent of what they call a 4A player in baseball. Good enough in a backup role, not good enough as a long term starter. Keenum’s only really good year as a starter came back in 2017, when he led the Minnesota Vikings to an 11-3 record in 14 starts. Keenum posted a 98 passer rating that year, with a 22:7 touchdown to interception ratio. Good stuff, but he was never able to repeat that magical run. Keenum started 16 games for the Denver Broncos the following year, but he led the team to just a 6-10 record with an 82 passer rating. In the ensuing 7+ years Keenum has made a total of just 13 NFL starts as he has settled into the steady veteran backup role.

Keenum is unlikely to put together a bunch of repeat performances following his great showing against the Eagles last week. Nonetheless he is a veteran with a ton of NFL experience. He may not have outstanding physical traits, but he knows how to play the game. With a career passer rating of 85 and an 81:51 career touchdown to interception ratio, Keenum is capable of giving a team competent if uninspiring play under center.

As for Bagent, who knows what he’s capable of? The last we saw of him in extended NFL play Bagent was a liability on the field. Is that still the case? There’s no way to be sure, but we’re about to find out. Bears head coach Ben Johnson is rightly credited with being an outstanding offensive mind, but he isn’t infallible. The Bears may have made a mistake choosing Bagent over Keenum this week. If so, the Jets need to take advantage of the opportunity. Maybe Aaron Glenn and company can confuse the inexperienced Bagent in a way that would be unlikely to succeed against the grizzled veteran Keenum. A possibly unready Bagent just might give the Jets the advantage in this game. Maybe even give the Jets an interception or two for the first time in ages. Let’s see what the Jets defense can cook up against the Bears’ young signal caller.

item.title: Week 4 Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's lineup advice
item.description: Justin Boone helps you set those lineups for fantasy football in Week 4.
item.content:encoded:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench. 

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 4 rankings. 

Starts

Tyler Shough, QB, Saints

vs. Falcons

Shough is off to an impressive start, posting the fourth-most fantasy points among quarterbacks so far. That includes very consistent production with weekly finishes as the QB6, QB8 and QB6 through three games. 

After fielding the fastest-paced offense last season, Kellen Moore has picked up where he left off. The Saints are nearly a full second quicker in neutral pace of play, which leads to plenty of volume for Shough and company. 

We're set up for a Monday night shootout, with a Falcons team that looked much more competitive with Michael Penix Jr. under center last week. Atlanta's defense is giving up the 12th-most fantasy points to passers and had to place its best cornerback A.J. Terrell on injured reserve. You can confidently project another QB1 result from Shough. 

Other QBs to start:

  • Jared Goff at Panthers – Speaking of corners heading to IR, Carolina just lost both Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson for at least the next four weeks and possibly longer. Even though we tend to avoid Goff when he's outdoors, we'll make an exception here in a game that's tied for the highest projected point total on the week at 51.5.

  • Bryce Young vs. Lions – Young is on the other side of that contest and facing a Lions defense that's been without several starters. Unsurprisingly, that's led to Detroit allowing the most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this year. Young is positioned well for his third top-12 finish on the season. 

Jeremiyah Love, RB, Cardinals

at Giants

Love is fresh off a breakout game against the 49ers, where he put up 109 scrimmage yards and a receiving touchdown on 26 touches. That was by far his strongest usage of the season (64% snap share) and a sign of things to come for the third overall pick. 

We might have even seen this happen sooner if it wasn't for his preseason ankle injury, but fantasy managers who drafted him in the third round aren't complaining now. 

Next up is a potential positive game script against a Giants defense that's given up the 10th-most fantasy points to running backs this season, including Javonte Williams (72 yards, two TDs), Kyren Williams (97 yards, one TD), Blake Corum (92 yards) and Tony Pollard (96 yards). Get ready for a big week from Love, who is a top-10 RB in my rest-of-season trade value charts.

Other RBs to start:

  • Aaron Jones Sr. vs. Dolphins – Jones, who turns 32 in December, can't hold up to massive workloads forever, but he should do well against a Miami team that's allowed the most fantasy points to running backs, including top-five finishes in each of the first three weeks. 

  • Braelon Allen at Bears – Breece Hall is sidelined, opening the door for the 22-year-old Allen, who's flashed on his limited touches. Chicago's defense has permitted at least 80 scrimmage yards to every starting RB its played. 

  • Jacory Croskey-Merritt vs. Colts (London) – Rachaad White is dealing with a shoulder injury that will keep him out this week. That may leave the recently signed Austin Ekeler and rookie Kaytron Allen as the only backups behind JCM. As I wrote about in my trade tips column, Bill is being underrated after a 48-yard TD was called back on an illegal formation penalty last week. I'm excited to see what he can do against a Colts defense that's the sixth-easiest matchup for RBs. 

Matthew Golden, WR, Packers

at Buccaneers

Golden is tied for the seventh-most targets per game through three weeks, just ahead of his teammate Christian Watson. While both players are performing well, Watson has received significantly more praise and sits as the WR3 overall in fantasy points per game. However, Golden isn't far behind at WR14. 

With the current state of Green Bay's offense, Watson and Golden are going to remain busy. The Packers have lost Jayden Reed for the season, Tucker Kraft is still working his way back to form after last year's ACL tear and the run game is non-existent. 

At the moment, Golden is looking like one of the best fantasy picks you could have made this summer. Expect his strong production to continue against Tampa's pass funnel defense. 

Other WRs to start:

  • Josh Downs at Commanders (London) – With Alec Pierce sidelined, the Colts have finally turned up the volume for Downs, who has 20 targets, 12 catches and 149 yards over the last two games. Now, he squares off with a Commanders secondary that's allowed the most fantasy points to receivers. 

  • Michael Wilson at Giants – After posting his best stat line of the young season (11-89-1 on 17 targets!), Wilson gets his easiest matchup so far in Week 4. The Giants defense has been responsible for a top-20 WR finish in each of the first three weeks and Wilson is next. 

  • Jameson Williams at Panthers – A high-scoring game against a defense that's missing its top two corners sounds like the perfect get-right spot for Williams. This will be a spike-week for the Lions' boom-or-bust wideout. 

Juwan Johnson, TE, Saints

vs. Falcons

Johnson has been an excellent late-round selection and an extremely consistent fantasy starter in the opening month. Among tight ends, he's fifth in receptions, sixth in yards and tied for first with three touchdowns. That's helped generate TE7, TE13 and TE5 weekly finishes. 

A friendly matchup with the Falcons awaits in Week 4. Atlanta is the seventh-most generous defense to fantasy tight ends, including allowing a league-high three touchdowns to the position through three games. 

Jordyn Tyson has one more week on IR and isn't immediately expected back, so Johnson will continue to be a strong fantasy TE1. 

Other TEs to start:

  • Kenyon Sadiq at Bears – Following his seven-catch, 105-yard, one-touchdown breakout last week, Sadiq was limited in practice with a back injury this week. As long as he's healthy, he'll be a top-12 TE option, with Adonai Mitchell and Mason Taylor still week-to-week.  

  • Darren Waller vs. Lions – Waller gets to take on the same Detroit defense that was responsible for Sadiq's massive stat line in Week 3. Not only are the Lions giving up the most fantasy points to the position, they've allowed six touchdowns to tight ends in three weeks. If Jalen Coker is limited or ruled out, that would push Waller even higher up my rankings.

Sits

Drake Maye, QB, Patriots

at Bills

During his rookie season, in the nine outings where Maye played at least 85% of the snaps, he never finished lower than QB17. Last year, we saw him combine that high floor with a high ceiling and he finished as the QB3 overall in fppg, while scoring less than 14 fantasy points only one time. 

This season, he's been under 13 fantasy points in all three outings and currently sits as the QB35. 

Yes, there have been injuries to A.J. Brown and the offensive line. The matchups have also been tougher (Seahawks, Steelers, Jaguars) after having an easier schedule in 2025. However, it's still hard to explain the disappearance of Maye's once high floor. 

Even against a softer opponent in the Bills, it's hard to trust Maye in your lineup until we see him turn this around. Though Buffalo allowed four TDs to Jared Goff, they held C.J. Stroud and Justin Herbert to QB15 and QB23 finishes, respectively.

I'm not dropping Maye, but I am sending him to my bench in the leagues where I have a decent streaming option. 

Other QBs to sit:

  • Justin Herbert at Seahawks – Herbert is also on the list of quarterbacks who have been massive disappointments in September. This doesn't look like a bounce-back week with Ladd McConkey likely to play through a foot injury and the Seahawks' defense waiting for them in Seattle. 

  • Bo Nix at 49ers – Nix finally stepped up for fantasy managers last week, in part thanks to a rushing touchdown. They all count though. We'll see if he can get the Broncos into scoring position as frequently against a 49ers defense allowing the eighth-fewest fantasy points to QBs. 

Omarion Hampton, RB, Chargers

at Seahawks

Hampton has been unspectacular in the early part of the season, saving his fantasy performances in the first two weeks by scoring touchdowns. That's important since his role in the passing game is limited and potentially shrinking. 

Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal had their usage increase, resulting in Hampton only running a route on 16% of the dropbacks in Week 3. While I'm not concerned about his job security, it is worrisome that we might be talking about a three-man committee in an offense that's stumbled so far. 

The Seahawks aren't a defense to target either, since they're giving up the fifth-fewest points to runners. The schedule also doesn't relent for the next couple months with matchups against the Broncos, Chiefs, Rams, Texans and Ravens. 

Hampton might have to be started depending on your roster, but he's more of a TD-or-bust RB3 right now.  

Other RBs to sit:

  • Rhamondre Stevenson at Bills – Stevenson might be slightly undervalued in terms of his rest-of-season value, since his usage rebounded after fumbling in Week 2. Unfortunately, he's another ball-carrier sharing his backfield in a struggling offense. He's a TD-or-bust RB3 in a game where the Pats could fall behind quickly. 

  • Tony Pollard at Ravens – While the Ravens have given up solid stat lines to the likes of Jonathan Taylor and Javonte Williams, we can project the same for Pollard in a game the Titans will likely trail. Scoring opportunities are also few and far between for Tennessee.  

  • J.K. Dobbins at 49ers – Dobbins has been held to 36 yards, 36 yards and 53 yards during his first three appearances this season. He only caught one pass and has yet to visit the end zone. He's just a low-ceiling fantasy option, with RJ Harvey soaking up all the pass-catching work. 

Emeka Egbuka, WR, Buccaneers

vs. Packers

Through three weeks, Egbuka's numbers haven't been terrible, especially when you consider the overall state of the Bucs' offense. Stat lines of 5-63-0, 3-16-1 and 5-62-0 aren't going to destroy your chances of winning a fantasy week, but they aren't going to lead you to victory either. 

Now, he'll have to build on those performances without the help of Baker Mayfield for the next few weeks. Jalon Daniels is an intriguing rookie backup, but expecting him to improve this offense is wishful thinking. 

So even in a positive matchup with the Packers, I have Egbuka ranked as a volatile WR3/flex option. 

Other WRs to sit:

  • Ladd McConkey/Quentin Johnston at Seahawks – McConkey is reportedly likely to play through a foot injury, but he’ll be at less than 100 percent and the matchup with the Seahawks is enough for me to bench him. Meanwhile, Johnston has been so bad this year that he would just be a risky WR3/flex option with McConkey banged up.

  • Rome Odunze vs. Jets – The Bears' passing game is being split four ways instead of three now that Kalif Raymond has a legitimate role. Odunze's average depth of target is nearly double his fellow receivers and he isn't getting many of the easy targets. That makes him a TD-or-bust WR4/flex. 

  • Xavier Worthy at Raiders – Worthy hasn't topped 25 yards this season. A big play is possible at any point, but he's a very dangerous flex swing with an extremely low floor for fantasy managers. 

Dalton Schultz, TE, Texans

vs. Cowboys

It turns out other defensive coordinators get to watch prior game film and after seeing Schultz catch 12 passes for 140 yards in Week 2, the Colts made it a priority to cover him last Sunday. The result was just three targets, three receptions and 30 yards. 

With Nico Collins expected to return this week, the volume scam for Schultz is over. The Cowboys have also held every tight end other than Isaiah Likely under 25 yards. 

While Schultz can still be started as a lower-end TE2 streamer, you should be able to find a better option.

Other TEs to sit:

  • Colston Loveland vs. Jets – Loveland isn't commanding the immense target share he had down the stretch last season. With the Bears being content to spread the ball around more, Loveland is just a risky TE2 until we see otherwise. New York's defense hasn't given up a touchdown to tight ends yet, with 44 yards being the highest output against it.  

  • Kyle Pitts Sr. at Saints – When Drake London is healthy, Pitts is an afterthought in the Falcons' passing attack. His stat lines of 0-0-0, 1-15-0 and 1-5-0 should have been reason enough for you to drop him this week.

Last week we watched as our Colts got in the win column against a still winless Houston Texans team. The game came down to the wire after three costly Daniel Jones turnovers, but the defense stepped up to stop a struggling Texans offense. It is always and I mean always a good thing to win against a divisional opponent, but it truly was an ugly win.

At this point I roll my eyes every time someone asks me to download another app, but this one really does improve the experience so much that even I am telling you that if you like to hang out here, chat, celebrate, commiserate, and argue in the comments, this app is actually worth your time. What we saw last week wasn’t great, but it was better than a loss. Perhaps the best news to come out of last week is that the Houston Texans offense is very, very bad and they’re considering giving quarterback CJ Stroud a long term, market setting extension after the season. That’s fantastic news, I hope they do! Regardless, this week Indy will play another opponent that appears to be at least partially hobbled on paper.

The Washington Commanders come into week four down star quarterback Jayden Daniels, star receiver Terry McLaurin, starting guard Sam Cosmi, and former Colt and current starting safety Nick Cross. All will miss today’s game due to injury. The Colts will just be down Keenan Allen.

I am skeptical that what we saw last week was a tide turning moment for the 2026 Colts, specifically a defensive unit that still doesn’t appear to have things figured out. I think the Commanders have the ability to win any Sunday with Marcus Mariota at the helm and international games are usually low scoring and always weird. Hopefully the Colts can take advantage of Washington’s injury situation and pull out a win in front of King Charles.

The Cincinnati Bengals return home licking their wounds only to find the Jacksonville Jaguars waiting for them. That includes last season when Jake Browning put together a game winning drive to shock them in Week 2 after Burrow went down with an injury.

Even moving away from the quarterbacks, there is plenty going on in this game. The Bengals are coming off their worst defensive performance of the season in a humbling loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. This Jacksonville offense is certainly the best they’ve faced all season, so we will see how they handle this well oiled play action attack.

The Jaguars defense may be looking to prove they are legit. So far they have not faced what many would consider a top end quarterback after facing off against the Cleveland Browns, Denver Broncos and New England Patriots. This Bengals offense was dealing outside of Burrow getting strip sacked to end the game.

If both sides of the ball for either of these teams start rolling at the same time then they have the ability to look like a scary juggernaut. It might come down to who shows up on Sunday.

item.content:encoded:
Steelers defensive lineman Derrick Harmon had to be carted off during Thursday night's loss to the Browns and it looks like it will be a little while before he's back on the field.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Harmon is expected to miss a few weeks with a foot injury. Injured reserve is a consideration for Harmon and he'd miss at least four games if the team goes that route.

The Steelers will play the Colts, Buccaneers, Saints and Browns before a bye in Week 9.

Harmon had 12 tackles, 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble in the first four weeks of the season. The 2025 first-rounder had 27 tackles, three sacks and a fumble recovery during his rookie season.

item.title: Report: Lions, Sam LaPorta break off contract extension talks
item.description: The chances of tight end Sam LaPorta hitting free agency next year are reportedly looking a little better.
item.content:encoded:
The chances of tight end Sam LaPorta hitting free agency next year are reportedly looking a little better.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that LaPorta and the Lions have broken off talks on a contract extension. The 2023 second-round pick is in the final year of his rookie deal.

LaPorta and the Lions could revisit talks later in the season or early in the offseason. The team could also use the franchise tag to hold onto LaPorta, so it's not a sure thing that he'll be talking to other teams come March.

LaPorta has 14 catches for 144 yards and a touchdown so far this season.
